entries.sanskrit:
नवमे भगवन्-मायादि- दृक्षोर् दर्शनं मुहुः ।

माया-शिशोर् लयाब्धौ च मुनेर् निर्वेश-निर्गमैः ॥

भगवतः परितोष-पूर्वकं तद् अपेक्षित-वर-दानं कथयितुम् आह, संस्तुत इत्य्-आदिना ॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
सूत उवाच—

संस्तुतो भगवान् इत्थं मार्कण्डेयेन धीमता ।  
नारायणो नर-सखः प्रीत आह भृगूद्वहम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
saṁstuto bhagavān itthaṁ  
mārkaṇḍeyena dhīmatā  
nārāyaṇo nara-sakhaḥ  
prīta āha bhṛgūdvaham
entries.literal_english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: The Supreme Lord Nārāyaṇa, the friend of Nara, was satisfied by the proper glorification offered by the intelligent sage Mārkaṇḍeya. Thus the Lord addressed that excellent descendant of Bhṛgu.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: आत्म-समाधिना चित्तैकाग्र्येण ॥२॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
श्री-भगवान् उवाच—

भो भो ब्रह्मर्षि-वर्योऽसि सिद्ध आत्म-समाधिना ।  
मयि भक्त्यानपायिन्या तपः-स्वाध्याय-संयमैः ॥
entries.transliteration:
bho bho brahmarṣi-varyo ’si  
siddha ātma-samādhinā  
mayi bhaktyānapāyinyā  
tapaḥ-svādhyāya-saṁyamaiḥ
word_for_word: the Supreme Personality of Godhead said
entries.literal_english: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: My dear Mārkaṇḍeya, you are indeed the best of all learned brāhmaṇas. You have perfected your life by practicing fixed meditation upon the Supreme Soul, as well as by focusing upon Me your undeviating devotional service, your austerities, your study of the Vedas and your strict adherence to regulative principles.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: वयं ते परितुष्टाः स्मेति बहु-वचनं सर्व-देवाभिप्रायेण । वर-देशाद् इत्य् एक-वचनं द्वयोर् ऐक्याभिप्रायेण । प्रतीच्छ गृहाण ॥३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
वयं ते परितुष्टाः स्म त्वद्-बृहद्-व्रत-चर्यया ।  
वरं प्रतीच्छ भद्रं ते वरदोऽस्मि त्वद्-ईप्सितम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
vayaṁ te parituṣṭāḥ sma  
tvad-bṛhad-vrata-caryayā  
varaṁ pratīccha bhadraṁ te  
vara-do ’smi tvad-īpsitam
entries.literal_english: We are perfectly satisfied with your practice of lifelong celibacy. Please choose whatever benediction you desire, since I can grant your wish. May you enjoy all good fortune.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: वरेण च्छन्दयता त्वया जितम् उत्कर्षो दर्शितः । मम तु वराकाङ्क्षा नास्तीत्य् आह—वरेणेति ॥४॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
श्री-ऋषिर् उवाच—

जितं ते देव-देवेश प्रपन्नार्ति-हराच्युत ।  
वरेणैतावतालं नो यद् भवान् समदृश्यत ॥
entries.transliteration:
jitaṁ te deva-deveśa  
prapannārti-harācyuta  
vareṇaitāvatālaṁ no  
yad bhavān samadṛśyata
entries.literal_english: The sage said: O Lord of lords, all glories to You! O Lord Acyuta, You remove all distress for the devotees who surrender unto You. That you have allowed me to see You is all the benediction I want.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
गृहीत्वाजादयो यस्य श्रीमत्-पादाब्ज-दर्शनम् ।  
मनसा योग-पक्वेन स भवान् मेऽक्षि-गोचरः ॥
entries.transliteration:
gṛhītvājādayo yasya  
śrīmat-pādābja-darśanam  
manasā yoga-pakvena  
sa bhavān me ’kṣi-gocaraḥ
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: द्रक्ष्ये द्रष्टुम् इच्छामि । लोक-पालैर् ब्रह्मादिभिः सहितोऽयं लोको जनो यया सद्-भिदां सति वस्तुनि भेदम् ॥६॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
अथाप्य् अम्बुज-पत्राक्ष पुण्य-श्लोक-शिखामणे ।  
द्रक्ष्ये मायां यया लोकः स-पालो वेद सद्-भिदाम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
athāpy ambuja-patrākṣa  
puṇya-śloka-śikhāmaṇe  
drakṣye māyāṁ yayā lokaḥ  
sa-pālo veda sad-bhidām
entries.literal_english: O lotus-eyed Lord, O crest jewel of renowned personalities, although I am satisfied simply by seeing You, I do wish to see Your illusory potency, by whose influence the entire world, together with its ruling demigods, considers reality to be materially variegated.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: तथेति द्रक्ष्यसीति । स ईश्वरः स्मयन् प्रागात् । षाठान्तरे क्रिय-विशेषणम् ॥७॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
सूत उवाच—

इतीडितोऽर्चितः कामम् ऋषिणा भगवान् मुने ।  
तथेति स स्मयन् प्रागाद् बदर्य्-आश्रमम् ईश्वरः ॥
entries.transliteration:
itīḍito ’rcitaḥ kāmam  
ṛṣiṇā bhagavān mune  
tatheti sa smayan prāgād  
badary-āśramam īśvaraḥ
entries.literal_english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: O wise Śaunaka, thus satisfied by Mārkaṇḍeya’s praise and worship, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, smiling, replied, “So be it,” and then departed for His hermitage at Badarikāśrama.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: तम् एवार्थं माया-दर्शन-रूपम् । अग्न्यादि-मूर्तिषु ॥८॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तम् एव चिन्तयन्न् अर्थम् ऋषिः स्वाश्रम एव सः ।  
वसन्न् अग्न्य्-अर्क-सोमाम्बु- भू-वायु-वियद्-आत्मसु ॥
entries.transliteration:
tam eva cintayann artham  
ṛṣiḥ svāśrama eva saḥ  
vasann agny-arka-somāmbu-  
bhū-vāyu-viyad-ātmasu
entries.literal_english: Thinking always of his desire to see the Lord’s illusory energy, the sage remained in his āśrama, meditating constantly upon the Lord within fire, the sun, the moon, water, the earth, air, lightning and his own heart and worshiping Him with paraphernalia conceived in his mind. But sometimes, overwhelmed by waves of love for the Lord, Mārkaṇḍeya would forget to perform his regular worship.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
ध्यायन् सर्वत्र च हरिं भाव-द्रव्यैर् अपूजयत् ।  
क्वचित् पूजां विसस्मार प्रेम-प्रसर-सम्प्लुतः ॥
entries.transliteration:
dhyāyan sarvatra ca hariṁ  
bhāva-dravyair apūjayat  
kvacit pūjāṁ visasmāra  
prema-prasara-samplutaḥ
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: माया-दर्शनम् आह—तस्येत्य्-आदिना ॥१०॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तस्यैकदा भृगु-श्रेष्ठ पुष्पभद्रा-तटे मुनेः ।  
उपासीनस्य सन्ध्यायां ब्रह्मन् वायुर् अभून् महान् ॥
entries.transliteration:
tasyaikadā bhṛgu-śreṣṭha  
puṣpabhadrā-taṭe muneḥ  
upāsīnasya sandhyāyāṁ  
brahman vāyur abhūn mahān
word_for_word: at the juncture of the day
entries.literal_english: O brāhmaṇa Śaunaka, best of the Bhṛgus, one day while Mārkaṇḍeya was performing his evening worship on the bank of the Puṣpabhadrā, a great wind suddenly arose.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: तं वायुम् अनु बलाहका मेघा अभवन्न् आविर् बभूवुः । ते च तडिद्भिः सहिता उच्चैः स्वनन्तो गर्जन्तः । अक्षो रथाङ्गं तद्वत् स्थविष्ठा अभितो वर्ष-धारा मुमुचुः ॥११॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तं चण्ड-शब्दं समुदीरयन्तं

बलाहका अन्व् अभवन् करालाः ।

अक्ष-स्थविष्ठा मुमुचुस् तडिद्भिः

स्वनन्त उच्चैर् अभि वर्ष-धाराः ॥
entries.transliteration:
taṁ caṇḍa-śabdaṁ samudīrayantaṁ  
balāhakā anv abhavan karālāḥ  
akṣa-sthaviṣṭhā mumucus taḍidbhiḥ  
svananta uccair abhi varṣa-dhārāḥ
entries.literal_english: That wind created a terrible sound and brought in its wake fearsome clouds that were accompanied by lightning and roaring thunder and that poured down on all sides torrents of rain as heavy as wagon wheels.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: चतुर् दिक्षु वर्तमानाः समुद्राः समीर-वेगेनोर्मयस् तैर् भूतलं ग्रसन्तः । उग्रा नक्रा येषु, महा-भया आवर्ता येषु, गभीरो घोषो येषु, ते च ते च ते च ॥१२॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
ततो व्यदृश्यन्त चतुः समुद्राः

समन्ततः क्ष्मा-तलम् आग्रसन्तः ।

समीर-वेगोर्मिभिर् उग्र-नक्र-

महा-भयावर्त-गभीर-घोषाः ॥
entries.transliteration:
tato vyadṛśyanta catuḥ samudrāḥ  
samantataḥ kṣmā-talam āgrasantaḥ  
samīra-vegormibhir ugra-nakra-  
mahā-bhayāvarta-gabhīra-ghoṣāḥ
entries.literal_english: Then the four great oceans appeared on all sides, swallowing up the surface of the earth with their wind-tossed waves. In these oceans were terrible sea monsters, fearful whirlpools and ominous rumblings.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: आत्मना सह जरा-युजादि-चतुर्-विधं जगद् अन्तर् बहिश् चोपतापितं वीक्ष्य । क्ष्मां जलाप्लुतां वीक्ष्य । मुनिः समत्रसद् भयं प्राप । केनोपतापितम् ? अद्भिः । कथं-भूताभिः ? अतिद्युभिर् अतिक्रान्ता द्यौर् याभिः । स्वरैश् च सूर्य-रश्मिभिर् वायुभिर् वेति शेषः । शत-ह्रदाभिश् च विद्युद्भिः । दीर्घत्वम् आर्षं छन्दोऽनुसारेण ॥१३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
अन्तर् बहिश् चाद्भिर् अति-द्युभिः खरैः

शतह्रदाभिर् उपतापितं जगत् ।

चतुर्-विधं वीक्ष्य सहात्मना मुनिर्

जलाप्लुतां क्ष्मां विमनाः समत्रसत् ॥
entries.transliteration:
antar bahiś cādbhir ati-dyubhiḥ kharaiḥ  
śatahradābhir upatāpitaṁ jagat  
catur-vidhaṁ vīkṣya sahātmanā munir  
jalāplutāṁ kṣmāṁ vimanāḥ samatrasat
word_for_word: all the inhabitants of the universe
entries.literal_english: The sage saw all the inhabitants of the universe, including himself, tormented within and without by the harsh winds, the bolts of lightning, and the great waves rising beyond the sky. As the whole earth flooded, he grew perplexed and fearful.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: प्रभञ्जनेनाघूर्णितं प्रकम्पितं वाः उदकं यस्मिन् सः । अप्य् अधाच्छादयाम् आस । समं सह ॥१४॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तस्यैवम् उद्वीक्षत ऊर्मि-भीषणः

प्रभञ्जनाघूर्णित-वार् महार्णवः ।

आपूर्यमाणो वरषद्भिर् अम्बुदैः

क्ष्माम् अप्यधाद् द्वीप-वर्षाद्रिभिः समम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
tasyaivam udvīkṣata ūrmi-bhīṣaṇaḥ  
prabhañjanāghūrṇita-vār mahārṇavaḥ  
āpūryamāṇo varaṣadbhir ambudaiḥ  
kṣmām apyadhād dvīpa-varṣādribhiḥ samam
entries.literal_english: Even as Mārkaṇḍeya looked on, the rain pouring down from the clouds filled the ocean more and more until that great sea, its waters violently whipped into terrifying waves by hurricanes, covered up all the earth’s islands, mountains and continents.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: स-क्ष्मान्तरिक्षं भूम्य्-अन्तरिक्ष-स्थ-प्राणि-सहितम् । स-दिवं स्वर्ग-स्थ-देव-सहितम् । भागणा ज्योतिर् गणास् तैः सहितम् । जटा विक्षिप्य विकीर्य ॥१५॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
स-क्ष्मान्तरिक्षं स-दिवं स-भा-गणं

त्रै-लोक्यम् आसीत् सह दिग्भिर् आप्लुतम् ।

स एक एवोर्वरितो महा-मुनिर्

बभ्राम विक्षिप्य जटा जडान्ध-वत् ॥
entries.transliteration:
sa-kṣmāntarikṣaṁ sa-divaṁ sa-bhā-gaṇaṁ  
trai-lokyam āsīt saha digbhir āplutam  
sa eka evorvarito mahā-munir  
babhrāma vikṣipya jaṭā jaḍāndha-vat
entries.literal_english: The water inundated the earth, outer space, heaven and the celestial region. Indeed, the entire expanse of the universe was flooded in all directions, and out of all its inhabitants only Mārkaṇḍeya remained. His matted hair scattered, the great sage wandered about alone in the water as if dumb and blind.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: परिश्रमेण इषितो गतः प्राप्त इत्य् अर्थः । इषु सर्पणे इत्य् अस्मात् ॥१६॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
क्षुत्-तृट्-परीतो मकरैस् तिमिङ्गिलैर्

उपद्रुतो वीचि-नभस्वताहतः ।

तमस्य् अपारे पतितो भ्रमन् दिशो

न वेद खं गां च परिश्रमेषितः ॥
entries.transliteration:
kṣut-tṛṭ-parīto makarais timiṅgilair  
upadruto vīci-nabhasvatāhataḥ  
tamasy apāre patito bhraman diśo  
na veda khaṁ gāṁ ca pariśrameṣitaḥ
entries.literal_english: Tormented by hunger and thirst, attacked by monstrous makaras and timiṅgila fish and battered by the wind and waves, he moved aimlessly through the infinite darkness into which he had fallen. As he grew increasingly exhausted, he lost all sense of direction and could not tell the sky from the earth.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: अन्योन्य-घातिभिस् तद्-भक्षणाय परस्परं युध्यद्भिः ॥१७॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
क्वचिन् मग्नो महावर्ते तरलैस् ताडितः क्वचित् ।  
यादोभिर् भक्ष्यते क्वापि स्वयम् अन्योन्य-घातिभिः ॥
entries.transliteration:
kracin magno mahāvarte  
taralais tāḍitaḥ kvacit  
yādobhir bhakṣyate kvāpi  
svayam anyonya-ghātibhiḥ
word_for_word: he was threatened with being eaten
entries.literal_english: At times he was engulfed by the great whirlpools, sometimes he was beaten by the mighty waves, and at other times the aquatic monsters threatened to devour him as they attacked one another. Sometimes he felt lamentation, bewilderment, misery, happiness or fear, and at other times he experienced such terrible illness and pain that he felt himself dying.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.main_sanskrit:
क्वचिच् छोकं क्वचिन् मोहं क्वचिद् दुःखं सुखं भयम् ।  
क्वचिन् मृत्युम् अवाप्नोति व्याध्य्-आदिभिर् उतार्दितः ॥
entries.transliteration:
kvacic chokaṁ kvacin mohaṁ  
kvacid duḥkhaṁ sukhaṁ bhayam  
kvacin mṛtyum avāpnoti  
vyādhy-ādibhir utārditaḥ

entries.sanskrit: श्रीमद्-रम्यं वदन-पङ्कजं यस्य तम् । कम्बुवत् त्रि-रेखावृता ग्रीवा यस्य तम् । महोरस्कं विशाल-वक्षसम् । सुनासं शोभना नासा यस्य तम् । सुन्दरे भ्रुवौ यस्य तम् ॥२२॥
entries.main_sanskrit:

word_for_word: महा-मरकत-श्यामं श्रीमद्-वदन-पङ्कजम् ।   कम्बु-ग्रीवं महोरस्कं सुनासं सुन्दर-भ्रुवम् ॥

The infant’s dark-blue complexion was the color of a flawless emerald, His lotus face shone with a wealth of beauty, and His throat bore marks like the lines on a conchshell. He had a broad chest, a finely shaped nose, beautiful eyebrows, and lovely ears that resembled pomegranate flowers and that had inner folds like a conchshell’s spirals. The corners of His eyes were reddish like the whorl of a lotus, and the effulgence of His corallike lips slightly reddened the nectarean, enchanting smile on His face. As He breathed, His splendid hair trembled and His deep navel became distorted by the moving folds of skin on His abdomen, which resembled a banyan leaf. The exalted brāhmaṇa watched with amazement as the infant took hold of one of His lotus feet with His graceful fingers, placed a toe within His mouth and began to suck.

entries.sanskrit: हृत्-पद्मं च विलोचनाम्बुजे च प्रोत्फुल्लानि तानि यस्य सः । अद्भुत-भावोऽत्य्-आश्चर्य-रूपं तेन शङ्कितः सन्न् अपि तं प्रष्टुं पुरः प्रससार समीपं गतः ॥२६॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तद्-दर्शनाद् वीत-परिश्रमो मुदा

प्रोत्फुल्ल-हृत्-पद्म-विलोचनाम्बुजः ।

प्रहृष्ट-रोमाद्भुत-भाव-शङ्कितः

प्रष्टुं पुरस् तं प्रससार बालकम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
tad-darśanād vīta-pariśramo mudā  
protphulla-hṛt-padma-vilocanāmbujaḥ  
prahṛṣṭa-romādbhuta-bhāva-śaṅkitaḥ  
praṣṭuṁ puras taṁ prasasāra bālakam
entries.literal_english: As Mārkaṇḍeya beheld the child, all his weariness vanished. Indeed, so great was his pleasure that the lotus of his heart, along with his lotus eyes, fully blossomed and the hairs on his body stood on end. Confused as to the identity of the wonderful infant, the sage approached Him.

entries.sanskrit: अद इदं जगद् यथा पुरा प्रलयात् पूर्वं न्यस्तं विन्यस्तं दृष्ट्वा चातीव विस्मितः सन्न् अमुह्यत ॥२७॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तावच् छिशोर् वै श्वसितेन भार्गवः

सोऽन्तः शरीरं मशको यथाविशत् ।

तत्राप्य् अदो न्यस्तम् अचष्ट कृत्स्नशो

यथा पुरामुह्यद् अतीव-विस्मितः ॥
entries.transliteration:

so ’ntaḥ śarīraṁ maśako yathāviśat  
tatrāpy ado nyastam acaṣṭa kṛtsnaśo  
yathā purāmuhyad atīva vismitaḥ
entries.literal_english: Just then the child inhaled, drawing Mārkaṇḍeya within His body like a mosquito. There the sage found the entire universe arrayed as it had been before its dissolution. Seeing this, Mārkaṇḍeya was most astonished and perplexed.

entries.sanskrit: कृत्स्नशो दर्शनं प्रपञ्चयति, खम् इत्य्-आदिना । ककुभो दिशः । पुराण्याकरांश् च । खेटान् कर्षक-ग्रामान् । व्रजान् गोकुलानि । आश्रमांश् च वर्णांश् च तेषां वृत्तीश् चेत्य् अर्थः ॥२८॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
खं रोदसी भा-गणान् अद्रि-सागरान्

द्वीपान् स-वर्षान् ककुभः सुरासुरान् ।

वनानि देशान् सरितः पुराकरान्

खेटान् व्रजान् आश्रम-वर्ण-वृत्तयः ॥
entries.transliteration:
khaṁ rodasī bhā-gaṇān adri-sāgarān  
dvīpān sa-varṣān kakubhaḥ surāsurān  
vanāni deśān saritaḥ purākarān  
kheṭān vrajān āśrama-varṇa-vṛttayaḥ
entries.literal_english: The sage saw the entire universe: the sky, heavens and earth, the stars, mountains, oceans, great islands and continents, the expanses in every direction, the saintly and demoniac living beings, the forests, countries, rivers, cities and mines, the agricultural villages and cow pastures, and the occupational and spiritual activities of the various social divisions. He also saw the basic elements of creation along with all their by-products, as well as time itself, which regulates the progression of countless ages within the days of Brahmā. In addition, he saw everything else created for use in material life. All this he saw manifested before him as if it were real.

entries.sanskrit: नाना-युगानि कल्पांश् च कल्पयति तैर् वा कल्प्यत इति तथा तं कालं च । सद् इव परमार्थ इवावभासितं तेनैव ॥२९॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
महान्ति भूतान्य् अथ भौतिकान्य् असौ

कालं च नाना-युग-कल्प-कल्पनम् ।

यत् किञ्चिद् अन्यद् व्यवहार-कारणं

ददर्श विश्वं सद् इवावभासितम् ॥

yat kiñcid anyad vyavahāra-kāraṇaṁ  
dadarśa viśvaṁ sad ivāvabhāsitam

निजाश्रमं यत्र ऋषी अपश्यत ।

विश्वं विपश्यञ् छ्वसिताच् छिशोर् वै

bahir nirasto nyapatal layābdhau

entries.sanskrit: तावत् परिष्वङ्ग-लाभात् पूर्वम् एव ऋषेस् तस्यान्तर्हितो बभूव । तद्-उद्यम-वैफल्ये दृष्टान्तः, अनीशो निर्दैवस् तेन निर्मिता ईहा क्रीडा यथेति ॥३३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तस्मिन् पृथिव्याः ककुदि प्ररूढं

वटं च तत्-पर्ण-पुटे शयानम् ।

तोकं च तत्-प्रेम-सुधा-स्मितेन

निरीक्षितोऽपाङ्ग-निरीक्षणेन ॥

अथ तं बालकं वीक्ष्य नेत्राभ्यां धिष्ठितं हृदि ।  
अभ्ययाद् अति-सङ्क्लिष्टः परिष्वक्तुम् अधोक्षजम् ॥
entries.transliteration:
tasmin pṛthivyāḥ kakudi prarūḍhaṁ  
vaṭaṁ ca tat-parṇa-puṭe śayānam  
tokaṁ ca tat-prema-sudhā-smitena  
nirīkṣito ’pāṅga-nirīkṣaṇena

atha taṁ bālakaṁ vīkṣya  
netrābhyāṁ dhiṣṭhitaṁ hṛdi  
abhyayād ati-saṅkliṣṭaḥ  
pariṣvaktum adhokṣajam
entries.literal_english: In that vast sea he again saw the banyan tree growing on the tiny island and the infant boy lying within the leaf. The child glanced at him from the corner of His eyes with a smile imbued with the nectar of love, and Mārkaṇḍeya took Him into his heart through his eyes. Greatly agitated, the sage ran to embrace the transcendental Personality of Godhead. In that vast sea he again saw the banyan tree growing on the tiny island and the infant boy lying within the leaf. Greatly agitated, the sage ran to embrace the transcendental Personality of Godhead.

entries.sanskrit: तावत् परिष्वङ्ग-लाभात् पूर्वम् एव ऋषेस् तस्यान्तर्हितो बभूव । तद्-उद्यम-वैफल्ये दृष्टान्तः, अनीशो निर्दैवस् तेन निर्मिता ईहा क्रीडा यथेति ॥३३॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तावत् स भगवान् साक्षाद् योगाधीशो गुहाशयः ।  
अन्तर्दध ऋषेः सद्यो यथेहानीश-निर्मिता ॥
entries.transliteration:
tāvat sa bhagavān sākṣād yogādhīśo guhāśayaḥ
antardadhe ṛṣeḥ sadyo yathehānīśa-nirmitā
entries.literal_english: Before the sage could obtain the embrace, the Lord, the direct Lord of yoga dwelling in the heart, disappeared at once, just as an endeavor made by one without power fails.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source range preserved.

entries.sanskrit: अन्तर्हितं भगवन्तम् अनु वटः सलिलं लोक-संप्लवश् च तिरो-धाय्य् अन्तर्हितः । स च स्वाश्रम एव यथा-पूर्वं स्थित इति ॥३४॥
entries.main_sanskrit:
तम् अन्व् अथ वटो ब्रह्मन् सलिलं लोक-सम्प्लवः ।  
तिरोधायि क्षणाद् अस्य स्वाश्रमे पूर्व-वत् स्थितः ॥
entries.transliteration:
tam anv atha vaṭo brahman  
salilaṁ loka-samplavaḥ  
tirodhāyi kṣaṇād asya  
svāśrame pūrva-vat sthitaḥ
entries.literal_english: After the Lord disappeared, O brāhmaṇa, the banyan tree, the great water and the dissolution of the universe all vanished as well, and in an instant Mārkaṇḍeya found himself back in his own hermitage, just as before.
